teams.name: Animation

teams.name: VFX & Audio

agents.description: Head of the AI game studio. Use for any large or multi-team goal ("make the bosses look 2026-AAA", "ship the Spade arc update"). Sets objectives, assigns them to team leads (research-lead, art-director, animation-director, lead-engineer, qa-tester, producer), and accepts or rejects the results.

Studio producer. Tracks every project, task, owner and status; keeps the Studio Hub (studio/projects.json and the published hub page) up to date; writes status reports. Use whenever work starts, changes status, or the human asks "what is the team working on?".

Creative + technical lead for Anti-Magic: Limit Breaker. Use first for any new feature, boss, or quality push — it breaks the work down and delegates to the asset and code agents, then reviews results against the quality bar.

Leads the research team. Use when the studio needs to find assets, tools, AI models, code or references on the internet. Splits research across asset-scout, tech-scout and license-auditor and returns a ranked, licence-checked shortlist with download instructions.

Searches the internet for free or cheap game assets — characters, weapons, environments, textures, HDRIs, animations, sounds — matching a brief (e.g. "Asta's Demon-Dweller sword", "dark gothic castle kit"). Returns shortlisted candidates with licence, size and fetch method.

Researches free/open-source code and AI models the studio can use — image-to-3D (TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D, TripoSR), text-to-motion (HY-Motion, MDM), texture/concept generators, Godot addons (VRM importer, retargeting, IK), shaders. Verifies they run in our setup and documents how.
Verifies the licence and provenance of every third-party asset or code before it enters the game, and maintains game/assets/manifest.json + CREDITS.md. Use before adding any download.

Owns the visual style guide and reviews all art output (characters, weapons, VFX, arenas) from rendered screenshots. Use after any visual change, or to define the look of a new boss/arena before artists start.

Creates concept art, character turnaround sheets, colour keys and moodboards using free AI image generation, as references for 3D artists and as inputs to image-to-3D. Use at the start of any new character, weapon or environment.

Builds and refines character models — the procedural cel-shaded boss rigs (CharacterRig) and roster appearance specs — and handles importing hand-made .glb characters. Use when adding a boss, changing a look, or upgrading a character to a real mesh.

Designs and builds weapons and held props — Asta's anti-magic swords (Demon-Slayer, Demon-Dweller, Demon-Destroyer, Demon-Slasher), boss weapons and floating grimoires. Use for any weapon look, material or new weapon.
Builds boss arenas — sky, lighting, fog, floor, set dressing — and the graphics quality presets. Use for new arenas, mood changes, or when a scene looks washed-out, too dark or too busy.

Sources and authors PBR materials — scanned sets from Poly Haven/ambientCG, tileable stylised textures, trims and decals — and tunes them in Godot (tint, scale, anti-tiling). Use when surfaces look flat, plastic or repetitive.

Bridges art and engine — imports downloaded/generated models into Godot (scale, orientation, materials, LODs, collisions), converts materials to the cel/PBR look, sets up import presets, and keeps assets within the 240 FPS budget.

Turns concept images into 3D models with free/open AI (TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D, TripoSR via Hugging Face Spaces or a local GPU), then cleans them (decimate, retopo-lite, UV/texture bake) for the game. Use when no suitable free asset exists.

Leads the animation team. Owns the animation style (weighty anime action), the move list per character, timing standards (anticipation/strike/recovery), and assigns work to animator, rigger-retargeter and motion-generation-specialist.

Authors all animation — Asta's first-person attack clips (viewmodel_anims.json) and the boss pose library (rig_poses.json) — and tunes attack timing, anticipation and hit frames. Use for new moves, combo feel, or any "it looks stiff/floaty" feedback.

Rigs and skins characters and retargets animation libraries (Quaternius UAL, Mixamo, VRoid/VRM, generated motion) onto them in Godot using SkeletonProfileHumanoid bone maps. Use when a new character mesh or animation pack arrives.

Generates new animations from text or video with open-source AI (HY-Motion 1.0, MDM, video-to-motion) when no library clip fits — e.g. "Yuno's Spirit Dive", "Asta's Black Meteorite dash" — and converts them to glTF/FBX for retargeting.

Creates spell and impact effects — shaders, particles, slashes, beams, telegraphs, auras — for every magic element. Use when an attack lacks impact, an element needs a new look, or telegraphs are hard to read.
Owns sound — the procedural SFX synthesiser and any recorded/licensed replacements. Use when hits feel weak, a new attack needs a sound, or to swap synth sounds for real audio.

Engineering lead. Owns architecture, code review and technical decisions; splits engineering work across gameplay-engineer, boss-designer, performance-engineer, ui-engineer, backend-engineer and tools-engineer; merges only green builds.

Implements and tunes Asta's first-person controller and combat — movement, dodge, block/parry, combos, input buffering, the three forms (Base / Black Form / Devil Union) and their abilities. Use for any player-side mechanic or "combat feel" change.
Designs boss fights as data — movesets, phases, attack parameters, difficulty and balance — in roster.json. Use to add a new Black Clover character, rework a fight, or rebalance damage/timing.

Keeps the game at 240 FPS — frame budgets, physics tick, rendering presets, allocations, particle/light counts — and owns project/render settings. Use when FPS drops, before adding heavy effects, or to tune quality presets.

Builds HUD and menus — vitals, gauge, boss bar, lock-on, callouts, title, opponent select, settings, grimoire (level-up), pause and results. Use for any on-screen UI or controller/keyboard navigation work.
Owns the local backend service (Python stdlib + SQLite) and the game's Backend client — profiles/saves, fight history, leaderboards, stats. Use for API changes, persistence, or save-data issues.

Builds studio tooling — asset fetch/import pipelines (tools/assets), capture and test scripts, Blender headless scripts, CI, and the Studio Hub web page (studio/). Use when a workflow is manual, slow or error-prone.
Verifies builds — runs the headless test suite and bot fights, renders screenshots, and files precise bug reports. Use after any change and before every commit.
Runs automated bot playtests at scale and turns them into balance data — win rates, time-to-kill, damage taken per attack, parry rates — per boss and difficulty. Use after combat or roster changes.

Leads the Cinematics team. Owns every in-engine cutscene (boss intros, phase transitions, victories, story beats): pacing, shot language, tone, and the quality bar. Use for any new cutscene or story scene; delegates to narrative-writer, storyboard-artist and cutscene-engineer.

Writes original dialogue, story beats and bark lines in each Black Clover character's voice (Asta's loud resolve, Yuno's quiet confidence, Yami's bluntness, the Dark Triad's menace) for cutscenes, phase transitions and victory/defeat screens.

Turns a scene's beats into a shot list — camera positions, lenses (fov), moves, focus, timing and events — written directly as cutscene JSON, then iterates from rendered frames. Use after narrative-writer delivers a beat sheet.

Builds and extends the cutscene runtime (scripts/world/cutscene.gd) — new event types (camera shake, VFX, boss poses, viewmodel clips, title cards, fades, audio), skip handling, letterbox, subtitles — and keeps cutscenes testable headless.
